checks.lead: Muhammad Ali (4 March 1769 – 2 August 1849) was an Ottoman viceroy who became the de facto ruler of Egypt from 1805 to 1848, and is widely considered the founder of modern Egypt. A governor of Albanian origin, Ali extended his control from Egypt to include Sudan, Hejaz, the Levant, Cyprus, Crete and parts of Greece at the height of his rule in 1840, and transformed Cairo from a mere Ottoman provincial capital to the center of an expansive empire.
